0.value:
The word_gate node passes only the words that are in its vocabulary, and drops the rest.

That is how you keep a text stream to a known set of words - useful when the words are going to drive something that only understands certain ones, and as a way of ignoring the noise in a recognition stream without having to list what to reject.

HOW IT READS THE TEXT:
The incoming text is broken into words at anything that is not a letter or an apostrophe, so numbers and punctuation never get through. Each word is looked up as it is, then in small letters. A word that is not in the vocabulary on its own can still pass as the second half of a two-word entry: with "new york" in the vocabulary, "New York" passes as one item.

The words that pass are sent as one string, joined by spaces. When nothing passes, nothing is sent.

THE VOCABULARY IS A DICTIONARY:
Each entry is a word and what to send in its place. 'include word' files a word under itself, so it passes unchanged. A dictionary arriving at 'dictionary in' replaces the vocabulary, and can map a word to something else: {"crimson": "red"} lets crimson through as red.

SYNTAX:
word_gate

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

string in:
The text to filter. Receiving it triggers the node.

dictionary in:
A dictionary that replaces the vocabulary.

load dictionary:
The path of a JSON file holding the vocabulary as a dictionary. Entering a path here, or sending one, loads it and replaces the vocabulary.

include word:
Adds to the vocabulary. A list adds each of its words; a single string is added whole, so a string node holding "new york" adds the two-word entry.

OUTPUTS:

gated string out:
The words that passed, or what the vocabulary maps them to.

RELATED:
word_trigger fires on particular words rather than passing them along. string_replace and dict_replace substitute without filtering anything out.
